**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 8, §8.6. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

A predictor with many features may fit training orders perfectly yet be brittle. Model selection weighs generalisation performance, complexity and measurement cost.

## Formal relationship

$$
\hat m=\arg\min_{m\in\mathcal M}\operatorname{CVRisk}(m)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Compare a model using only distance against a model using distance, item count and dozens of polynomial features. Fit each on training folds and evaluate it on held-out folds. Choose the one with better validation performance, then assess the selected model on untouched test data.

## Interpretation and limitations

The same test set must not be repeatedly used to tune models without biasing the estimate. Cross-validation splits must respect temporal order when future delivery demand is the target.

## Explain it yourself

Why is random shuffling potentially misleading if the training data are last month's orders and the goal is predicting next month?
